explain.say: Every person, including you, started as a single cell smaller than a full stop. Nine months later, a baby with billions of cells was born! Let's walk along the timeline of a pregnancy.

faq.a: Fertilisation is when the nucleus of a sperm cell joins with the nucleus of an egg cell. The new cell, called a zygote, has 46 chromosomes: 23 from each parent.
About a week after fertilisation, the tiny ball of cells, called an embryo, attaches to the thick lining of the uterus, where it can get food and grow.

faq.q: What is the difference between an embryo and a fetus?
faq.a: In the first weeks the developing baby is called an embryo. From about week 10 of pregnancy, once the main organs have started to form, it is called a fetus.
asks: Tell me about the organs forming

faq.a: The placenta lets food and oxygen pass from the mother's blood to the baby's blood and lets waste like carbon dioxide pass back, without the two blood supplies mixing. The umbilical cord connects it to the baby.
About 40 weeks, or nine months, counted from the first day of the mother's last period. Babies born before 37 weeks are called premature.
asks: How many weeks is a pregnancy?

facts: A full-term pregnancy is about 40 weeks, counted from the first day of the last menstrual period.
The placenta allows exchange of food, oxygen and waste between mother and fetus without their blood mixing.
Newborn babies have about 300 bones; many fuse together, leaving 206 in adults.

options.show: Passes food and oxygen from mother to baby
options.say: Passes food and oxygen from mother to baby

quiz.why: The placenta exchanges food, oxygen and waste between mother and baby.

wrong.1: Bones grow from the baby's own cells.
wrong.2: The baby has its own heart that pumps its blood.

quiz.show: How many chromosomes does a fertilised egg have?
quiz.why: It gets 23 from the sperm and 23 from the egg, making 46.
